name: Permutation Counting
description: You have some cards. An integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$n$$$ is written on each card: specifically, for each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, you have $$$a_i$$$ cards which have the number $$$i$$$ written on them. There is also a shop which contains unlimited cards of each type. You have $$$k$$$ coins, so you can buy $$$k$$$ new cards in total, and the cards you buy can contain any integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$n$$$. After buying the new cards, you rearrange all your cards in a line. The score of a rearrangement is the number of (contiguous) subarrays of length $$$n$$$ which are a permutation of $$$[1, 2, \ldots, n]$$$. What's the maximum score you can get?
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t\ (1\le t\le 100)$$$. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ ($$$1\le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0\le k \le 10^{12}$$$) — the number of distinct types of cards and the number of coins. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^{12}$$$) — the number of cards of type $$$i$$$ you have at the beginning. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single line containing an integer: the maximum score you can get.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1967A — Permutation Counting [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
